jsurvival

Abstract

jsurvival provides time-to-event analyses and data preparation in jamovi and R, as part of the ClinicoPath suite. Its nine analyses cover Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cox and Fine-Gray regression, exploratory LASSO Cox modeling, odds ratios, dates and endpoint recoding. Results support research analysis; clinical interpretation depends on the endpoint definition, study design, data quality and model assumptions.

🎯 Key Features & Analysis Suite (9 Analyses)

jsurvival provides 9 dedicated analyses under the Survival menu in jamovi:

Analysis Function Category Key Clinical Features
Survival Analysis survival Core Time-to-Event Kaplan-Meier estimation, log-rank comparisons between groups, Cox proportional hazards regression, median survival with CIs, 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival rates, person-time calculations, and publication-ready risk tables.
Single Arm Survival singlearm Cohort Follow-up Cohort-wide survival analysis for single-arm clinical trials or registry cohorts without an explanatory group; includes milestone survival rates, and person-time metrics.
Multivariable Survival multisurvival Advanced Modeling Multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling with covariate adjustment, Fine-Gray regression for competing events, hazard ratio forest plots, model diagnostics, and adjusted survival curves.
Continuous Survival survivalcont Biomarker Thresholds Survival analysis for continuous variables and biomarkers; features a data-derived cut-off (maximally selected rank statistic, with a p-value adjusted for the search; it needs independent validation), multiple cut-offs by quantile, recursive, tree or minimum-p methods, and Kaplan-Meier plots by group.
Odds Ratio Analysis oddsratio Association Studies Logistic-regression odds ratios with profile-likelihood confidence intervals, optional Firth penalized estimation, forest plot, prediction nomogram and optional diagnostic metrics. Both outcome levels are named explicitly.
LASSO-Cox Regression lassocox High-Dimensional Modeling L1-penalized Cox regression via glmnet for high-dimensional feature selection (clinical, molecular, genomic), k-fold cross-validation, optimal lambda selection, and coefficient path plots.
Time Interval Calculator timeinterval Clinical Data Prep Robust calculation of follow-up durations from diagnosis and event/censoring dates, supporting days, weeks, months, and years with date sequence and consistency checks.
DateTime Converter datetimeconverter Clinical Data Prep Flexible date and timestamp parsing, standardization, and conversion into standardized temporal formats required for time-to-event analysis.
Outcome Organizer outcomeorganizer Endpoint Derivation Clinical endpoint mapping and standardization, recoding event statuses into analysis-ready indicators for OS, cause-specific, competing-risk, RFS, PFS, DFS, TTP and multistate analyses.

🚀 Installation

In jamovi

  1. Open jamovi (>= 2.7.27).
  2. Click the + button in the top-right corner → jamovi library.
  3. Search for jsurvival and install the available library version.

For a release candidate supplied by the maintainer, use Sideload in the module library and select its .jmo file. A local candidate may differ from the library version.

As an R Package 

# Install from GitHub
remotes::install_github("sbalci/jsurvival")

💡 Quick Start (R Interface) 

library(jsurvival)
data("melanoma", package = "jsurvival")
# status: 1 = died of melanoma, 2 = alive, 3 = died of other causes. time is in days.
# Only status 1 is an event here, so other-cause deaths are censored (cause-specific).

# 1. Kaplan-Meier, log-rank and Cox by group
fit <- jsurvival::survival(
  data = melanoma, elapsedtime = "time",
  outcome = "status", outcomeLevel = "1",
  dod = NULL, dooc = NULL, awd = NULL, awod = NULL,
  explanatory = "sex",
  timetypeoutput = "days", cutp = "365, 1095, 1825"
)

# 2. Continuous variable, with a data-derived cut-off
cut_fit <- jsurvival::survivalcont(
  data = melanoma, elapsedtime = "time",
  outcome = "status", outcomeLevel = "1",
  dod = NULL, dooc = NULL, awd = NULL, awod = NULL,
  contexpl = "age", findcut = TRUE,
  timetypeoutput = "days", cutp = "365, 1095, 1825"
)

# 3. LASSO Cox
data("lassocox_breast_cancer", package = "jsurvival")
lasso_fit <- jsurvival::lassocox(
  data = lassocox_breast_cancer, elapsedtime = "survival_months",
  outcome = "death", outcomeLevel = "Dead", censorLevel = "Alive",
  explanatory = c("age", "tumor_size_cm", "grade", "stage", "lymph_nodes_positive",
                  "er_status", "pr_status", "her2_status", "ki67_percent", "lvi"),
  lambda = "lambda.min"
)

Before reporting results

  • Use one row per independent patient. Recurrent events, repeated visits, delayed entry and time-dependent covariates require analyses designed for those data.
  • DateTime Converter parsing-count percentages use all observations; its separate parse rate excludes originally missing values. Successful parsing does not establish that the chosen date order is correct.
  • Confirm the event value and censoring rule. Missing status or a missing death date does not establish that a patient is alive. Composite endpoints need time to the first qualifying event; Outcome Organizer produces the status, not that time.
  • Precalculated follow-up is used in its supplied unit. Changing Time Type in Output does not convert it. Landmark analyses retain only times strictly greater than the landmark.
  • Use cumulative incidence for absolute event risk with competing events. A Cox HR, Fine-Gray subdistribution HR, odds ratio, rate and probability have different meanings.
  • Treat data-derived cutoffs and LASSO selection as exploratory. Preserve the exact cutoff (Low ≤ cutoff; High > cutoff). Lambda cross-validation tunes the penalty; displayed C-indices and same-data risk groups do not establish validated predictive performance.

The methods and reporting guide includes executable arithmetic checks and a reporting checklist. Read the 1.1.3 corrections before reusing results from earlier versions. Known limits include exploratory cutoff selection and apparent model performance. Multivariable Survival interaction forests show every fitted coefficient, conditioning values and a caption; interaction rows are ratios of hazard ratios, not subgroup HRs. Both forest styles use this coefficient display for interaction models. Survival Analysis adjusted curves use the age-adjusted table’s fitted model, retaining requested baseline and age-group strata. Stratified standardized curves end at the shortest observed stratum follow-up; confidence bands for these averages are not provided.

Example data

In jamovi, open ☰ → Open → Data Library → jsurvival → histopathology including analysis. It holds a simulated cohort, with invented patient names, and a saved analysis: Time Elapsed = OverallTime (months), Outcome = Outcome, Event Level = 1. From R, histopathology, melanoma and six lassocox_* datasets are available.

Nine additional .omv examples, one for every analysis, are saved in data/ and registered in jamovi/0000.yaml. Each contains synthetic data and an analysis configured and saved in the jamovi GUI. The example guide lists the files, saved arguments, checks and known display limitation. Open a file directly, or select its descriptive title in the module’s Data Library after rebuilding/installing the updated module. The odds-ratio example deliberately demonstrates the Firth nomogram safeguard; it is not a survival-risk analysis.
